PC: Assess and manage the patient’s airway by verifying patency, evaluating the presence and effort of breathing, and initiating appropriate oxygen supplementation as needed (via nasal cannula, facemask, high-flow nasal cannula, CPAP or BiPAP)
Initiate cardiopulmonary monitoring (if not on monitor already) and correctly identify the presence of sinus tachycardia, tachypnea, persistent hypoxia, and hypotension
Establish IV access; if peripheral IV cannot be established rapidly ( < 90 seconds) then intraosseous access must be obtained
Initiate fluid resuscitation in the setting of neonatal shock; appreciate that the patient continues to have persistent tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypoxia despite subsequent fluid resuscitation

Initiate the correct therapy for a ductal dependent congenital cardiac lesion by starting continuous infusion of prostaglandin E1 (with a dose of 0.025 to 0.05 mcg/kg/min and titrating as needed to a maximum dose of 0.1 mcg/kg/min)

Anticipate the respiratory consequences (i.e., apnea) of prostaglandin administration by preparing/performing intubation utilizing appropriate technique; recognize that the obtunded or moribund patient may need no sedative medications to accomplish intubation.
MK: Verbalize a differential diagnosis for neonatal shock including sepsis, ductal dependent lesions, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, and metabolic disorders.
Identify the neonate with critical coarctation of the aorta by diminished/absent femoral pulses, persistent hypoxia, and discordant blood pressures of the upper and lower extremities
SBP: Involve Cardiology and/or Cardiothoracic Surgery in the care of the patient who will need eventual corrective cardiac surgery
